title: Remove ballpoint ink from washable cotton
steps: Place a clean absorbent cloth beneath the stain and blot excess ink; dab a small amount of rubbing alcohol onto a hidden seam first.
If colourfast, dab ink gently from the outside in with alcohol on a white cloth, changing cloth sections frequently.
Rinse thoroughly and wash to the care label; air-dry until the mark has gone.
caution: Alcohol is flammable. Ventilate, keep away from flames, and avoid on acetate, delicate or dry-clean-only fabrics.

title: Remove washable marker stains
steps: Blot fresh marker with a damp white cloth rather than rubbing; check garment label.
Apply a little liquid laundry detergent to the stain and leave for 10 minutes.
Rinse and launder as directed; repeat before tumble drying if needed.
caution: Permanent markers may not fully lift. Test dyes first.

title: Remove coffee from a shirt
steps: Blot excess coffee with paper towel without spreading it; rinse from the back with cool water.
Work a small amount of liquid laundry detergent into the mark and leave 10 minutes.
Wash according to care label and inspect before drying.
caution: Milk or cream in coffee may need enzyme detergent; check fabric suitability.

title: Remove tea stains from table linen
steps: Blot fresh tea and flush stain from reverse with cool water; avoid rubbing.
Pre-treat with suitable laundry detergent for 10–15 minutes.
Wash at the hottest temperature permitted by the care label.
caution: Test coloured linen before using any stain remover.

title: Remove red wine from washable fabric
steps: Blot up liquid promptly using clean white cloths; keep the area from spreading.
Rinse from the back with cool water and apply suitable liquid laundry detergent.
Launder following care label and check before heat drying.
caution: Do not use bleach on coloured or delicate fabrics unless explicitly permitted.

title: Remove chocolate stains
steps: Scrape off excess chocolate gently with a spoon; let any melted chocolate firm up first.
Rinse from reverse with cool water and work in enzyme laundry detergent if fabric permits.
Wash according to label and check before drying.
caution: Hot water can set protein-containing food stains; check care label.

title: Remove tomato sauce stains
steps: Lift off sauce with a spoon without rubbing it deeper; rinse the reverse with cool water.
Apply liquid laundry detergent and let sit 10 minutes.
Wash normally and repeat treatment before drying if colour remains.
caution: Test any oxygen-based stain remover on an inconspicuous spot.

title: Remove grease from clothing
steps: Blot fresh oil with paper towel and avoid rubbing; check care label.
Work a drop of washing-up liquid into the mark gently, then rinse thoroughly.
Launder as directed and air-dry to check result.
caution: Washing-up liquid can cause excess foam in washing machines: rinse it out before machine washing.

title: Remove makeup foundation from collars
steps: Lift excess makeup with a dry tissue without smearing; check garment care label.
Dab a little liquid laundry detergent into the mark with fingers.
Wash according to label and check before drying.
caution: Test first on silk, wool and dark dyes; specialist cleaning may be safer.

title: Remove lipstick from washable fabric
steps: Scrape excess lipstick gently with a dull edge; do not spread.
Pre-treat with liquid detergent and gently blot with a clean cloth.
Rinse and wash following garment instructions.
caution: Lipstick dyes may remain; avoid harsh solvents on delicate fabrics.

title: Remove grass stains
steps: Brush off loose dirt and rinse garment with cool water; check label.
Rub in enzyme laundry detergent if the fabric allows and leave for 15 minutes.
Wash following care label and inspect before tumble drying.
caution: Do not use enzyme products on wool or silk unless the label permits.

title: Remove mud from trousers
steps: Let wet mud dry completely to avoid spreading; brush off loose dried mud outdoors.
Rinse from the back and pre-treat remaining marks with laundry detergent.
Wash according to garment label.
caution: Avoid aggressive brushing on delicate fabrics.

title: Remove blood from washable fabric
steps: Rinse the fresh stain promptly from the back using cold water; blot rather than rub.
Apply a small amount of suitable liquid detergent and leave briefly.
Wash on a suitable cool cycle and check before drying.
caution: Use gloves when cleaning blood that is not your own. Never use hot water initially.

title: Remove sweat marks from shirts
steps: Check the care label and test treatment on an inside seam; dampen affected area.
Pre-treat with suitable liquid laundry detergent and leave 15 minutes.
Wash following care label and air-dry.
caution: Some deodorant discoloration is permanent; avoid chlorine bleach on protein stains.

title: Remove berry juice stains
steps: Blot and rinse the stain from the reverse with cool running water; avoid scrubbing.
Apply laundry detergent to the damp area and let sit 10 minutes.
Wash as directed; inspect before drying.
caution: Colourfastness matters on bright garments; test first.

title: Clean fresh water-based paint from tile
steps: Keep children and pets away from spill; blot paint with paper towel while still wet.
Wipe tile with warm water and a little washing-up liquid using a soft cloth.
Rinse with clean water and dry the floor to prevent slipping.
caution: Do not use abrasive tools on glazed or delicate tile; test grout first.

title: Remove wet emulsion paint from clothing
steps: Scrape off excess wet paint carefully without pushing into fibres; rinse from reverse promptly.
Work a little liquid laundry detergent into the stain with cool water.
Rinse and wash according to label before paint dries.
caution: Dried paint may be permanent. Check paint label; do not use solvents indiscriminately.

title: Lift dried water-based paint from glass
steps: Check that glass has no protective coating or tint; soften spot with warm soapy water.
Gently work at paint using a plastic scraper held flat against the glass.
Wipe with damp cloth and dry.
caution: Avoid metal blades on coated glass; scratches and coating damage are possible.

title: Clean fresh oil-based paint from brushes
steps: Read the paint tin for its recommended brush cleaner; protect workspace and wear suitable gloves.
Wipe excess paint into a disposable rag then use the specified cleaner in a ventilated area.
Collect used solvent and paint residue for disposal per local council guidance.
caution: Solvents can be flammable and harmful; never pour them down drains or mix chemicals.

title: Remove paint splashes from laminate floor
steps: Identify paint type and test any method on a hidden area; lift wet paint with a damp cloth.
For dried water-based paint, soften briefly with a slightly damp cloth and use a plastic scraper gently.
Dry immediately and check the floor finish.
caution: Do not soak laminate or use strong solvents that may damage the coating.

title: Clean spilled wallpaper paste
steps: Scoop up thick paste promptly with a plastic card; protect nearby electrical outlets.
Wipe washable surface with a damp sponge, changing water frequently.
Dry and check for sticky residue after surface is dry.
caution: Do not saturate wallpaper, wood or electrical fittings.

title: Remove dried PVA glue from glass
steps: Check glass is plain uncoated glass and not a display screen; dampen glue with warm water.
Let it soften, then lift carefully with a plastic scraper.
Wipe with clean damp cloth and dry.
caution: Avoid sharp metal blades and abrasive pads on coated glass.

title: Clean plaster dust after decorating
steps: Ventilate the room and use a suitable vacuum with a fine-dust/HEPA filter if available.
Vacuum high surfaces and edges first, then wipe remaining dust with a slightly damp microfibre cloth.
Change cloths and rinse hard floors as needed.
caution: Avoid dry sweeping that sends fine dust airborne; wear appropriate dust protection.

title: Remove silicone sealant smears from tiles
steps: Allow sealant to cure if the product instructions recommend it; protect surrounding grout.
Lift the bulk gently using a plastic scraper and follow sealant maker's approved remover instructions.
Wipe residue and rinse as directed by the remover label.
caution: Test removers on a hidden spot; do not use on natural stone without checking compatibility.

title: Remove burnt food from a saucepan
steps: Let pan cool fully and remove loose burnt food with a wooden spoon.
Cover burnt area with warm water and washing-up liquid and soak for 30 minutes.
Use a non-scratch sponge; repeat soaking instead of aggressive scraping.
caution: Do not pour cold water into a very hot pan or use abrasive pads on non-stick coatings.

title: Clean sticky syrup spills
steps: Lift excess syrup with a spoon or absorbent cloth; prevent slip hazards.
Wipe washable surface with warm water and a small amount of washing-up liquid.
Rinse with a clean damp cloth and dry completely.
caution: Do not flood wooden floors or electrical surfaces.

title: Remove cooking oil from tiled floor
steps: Keep people off slippery area and blot up oil with paper towels.
Wash the tile with warm water and a little degreasing washing-up liquid.
Rinse thoroughly and dry, checking for remaining slick patches.
caution: Avoid mixing cleaners; be careful on porous stone or unsealed grout.

title: Remove curry stains from plastic food tubs
steps: Wash container with warm soapy water and check manufacturer care instructions.
Leave container in daylight briefly if suitable, then wash again with mild detergent.
Rinse and dry; repeat if needed.
caution: Discolouration can be permanent. Do not use harsh solvents on food-contact plastic.

title: Clean spilled milk from upholstery
steps: Blot milk immediately with a clean towel without rubbing; check upholstery care code.
If water cleaning is allowed, dab gently with a little mild detergent solution.
Blot with clean damp cloth and dry quickly with airflow.
caution: Do not soak foam cushions; seek professional help for delicate or dry-clean-only upholstery.

title: Remove melted chocolate from carpet
steps: Let chocolate harden, then lift solid pieces gently with a blunt spoon.
Blot remaining stain with upholstery/carpet-safe detergent following label.
Remove detergent residue with a lightly damp cloth and dry.
caution: Test colourfastness first; avoid excessive moisture or heat.

title: Clean spilled flour from kitchen floor
steps: Keep area dry initially; collect loose flour using dustpan or suitable vacuum.
Once loose powder is removed, wipe floor with a lightly damp cloth.
Rinse cloth and dry floor fully.
caution: Adding water to large amounts of flour makes a sticky paste.

title: Remove sticker residue from glass jars
steps: Peel paper label off and soak jar in warm soapy water if safe.
Rub softened adhesive gently with a cloth and a little cooking oil if needed.
Wash thoroughly with washing-up liquid and rinse.
caution: Keep oils off labels you wish to retain; do not use on porous surfaces.

title: Remove tape residue from painted doors
steps: Test in an inconspicuous spot and gently warm residue with your hand or warm damp cloth.
Roll adhesive off with fingertips or a soft cloth without scraping paint.
Wipe gently with mild soapy water and dry.
caution: Strong solvents and heat guns can remove paint; avoid them.

title: Remove chewing gum from washable fabric
steps: Place garment in a bag and chill in freezer until gum hardens.
Gently lift hardened gum with a blunt spoon without pulling threads.
Pre-treat residue with suitable laundry detergent and wash as labelled.
caution: Check fabric can tolerate freezing and do not force delicate fibres.

title: Remove candle wax from hard surfaces
steps: Let wax cool and harden completely; do not handle hot wax.
Lift gently with plastic scraper and wipe remaining film with warm soapy cloth if safe.
Dry and inspect finish.
caution: Avoid heat and scraping on varnished wood, painted surfaces and porous stone.

title: Remove candle wax from washable tablecloth
steps: Let wax harden and gently crumble off excess without tearing fabric.
Follow fabric-care guidance for remaining wax; use absorbent paper and low controlled warmth only if fabric permits.
Pre-treat oily residue with detergent and wash as labelled.
caution: Heat can damage synthetics and set dye; do not use iron on unknown fabrics.

title: Remove limescale from a chrome tap
steps: Check tap manufacturer guidance and avoid acidic cleaners if finish is sensitive.
Apply an approved limescale remover to a cloth rather than soaking fittings; follow label contact time.
Rinse promptly and dry with soft cloth.
caution: Acid can damage plated finishes and stone; never mix with bleach.

title: Clean grout discoloration
steps: Brush away loose debris and check whether grout is sealed or damaged.
Use a grout-safe cleaner according to its label and scrub gently with soft brush.
Rinse and dry well; improve ventilation.
caution: Dark staining may be mould or permanent staining; seek professional help for widespread mould.

title: Remove hard-water spots from shower screen
steps: Check coating instructions and start with warm soapy water and soft cloth.
If permitted, use a glass-safe limescale cleaner for the label's contact time.
Rinse completely and dry with a squeegee.
caution: Never combine acid-based descalers with bleach or chlorine cleaners.

title: Remove water rings from varnished wood
steps: Identify whether finish is varnish, wax or oil and test an inconspicuous area.
Gently buff with a dry soft cloth; use only a furniture-care product approved for the finish.
Stop if finish becomes cloudy or soft and consult a furniture specialist.
caution: Do not apply heat, abrasives or household acids to valuable furniture.

title: Remove crayon marks from painted walls
steps: Test paint washability on a hidden area and gently dust off loose material.
Wipe lightly with a soft cloth and mild soapy water without scrubbing.
Dab dry and repeat cautiously if paint is stable.
caution: Matt paint may mark or lift; avoid abrasive sponges.

title: Remove shoe scuffs from vinyl flooring
steps: Sweep grit away and test on hidden patch.
Rub mark gently with soft damp cloth and diluted floor-safe cleaner.
Rinse lightly and dry.
caution: Avoid solvents and abrasive pads that can dull vinyl.

title: Remove biro marks from faux leather
steps: Check maker's care instructions and test mild soapy water on hidden area.
Dab gently with soft cloth; stop if finish transfers or changes.
Dry promptly and consult specialist cleaner for persistent ink.
caution: Alcohol and solvents can strip faux-leather coating.

title: Remove pet paw prints from upholstery
steps: Let wet muddy prints dry if needed and vacuum loose grit using upholstery attachment.
If care code permits, dab with mild upholstery-safe cleaner using a white cloth.
Blot moisture and air-dry fully.
caution: Do not saturate cushions or use water on solvent-clean-only fabrics.

title: Remove bird droppings from patio furniture
steps: Wear gloves and dampen droppings to avoid making dust airborne.
Lift with disposable paper towels then clean with mild detergent suitable for furniture.
Rinse and dry; wash hands thoroughly.
caution: Do not dry-brush droppings or mix disinfectants; check material care.

title: Remove rust-coloured marks from paving
steps: Identify paving material and test a specialist product on hidden area.
Use only a rust remover explicitly approved for that stone or paving, following label.
Rinse as directed and protect nearby plants.
caution: Acidic products can etch limestone, marble and concrete; consult a professional if unsure.

title: Remove sticky tree sap from car paint
steps: Wash grit away first with automotive shampoo and water.
Use a dedicated automotive sap remover suitable for the finish following product instructions.
Rinse and dry with clean microfibre cloth.
caution: Do not scrape or use household solvents on automotive clear coat.

title: Remove insect marks from car windscreen
steps: Soak marks with water or automotive glass cleaner and let soften briefly.
Wipe with clean microfibre cloth using light pressure.
Rinse and inspect visibility before driving.
caution: Avoid abrasive pads and keep cleaners away from sensitive coatings.

title: Clean dried salt marks from shoes
steps: Check whether shoes are leather, suede or fabric and follow maker's care guidance.
For washable fabric, gently dab with a lightly damp cloth and mild shoe-safe cleaner.
Allow to air-dry away from direct heat.
caution: Do not wet suede heavily; use a specialist suede brush or cleaner.

title: Remove sticky drink spill from car cupholder
steps: Remove loose items and blot liquid before it reaches electrical controls.
Use a barely damp cloth with mild detergent on removable washable inserts.
Rinse inserts separately and dry completely before refitting.
caution: Do not pour liquid into car trim or near electronics.
